modules.title: Business spreadsheet formulas and checks
modules.summary: Formulas, cell references, summaries, and checks for a business worksheet.

sections.heading: Build the calculation before the formatting
paragraphs: Start by identifying which columns are inputs and which are calculated outputs. Keep units consistent: a percentage entered as 0.08 represents eight percent when formatted as a percentage. Multiplication and division occur before addition and subtraction unless parentheses change the order. A formula such as =B2*C2 calculates line revenue. SUM adds a range; AVERAGE computes its arithmetic mean; COUNT counts numeric values, while COUNTA counts nonempty cells. Blank cells and zero values have different meanings, so inspect missing data before calculating an average.

sections.heading: Choose functions and cell references
paragraphs: IF selects an output based on a condition; COUNTIF counts matching records; SUMIF totals records matching a condition. A lookup retrieves a related value using a key. Confirm whether an exact match is required and what happens when the key is missing. Relative references move when copied, absolute references hold both row and column, and mixed references hold one. Use a fixed reference for a shared assumption such as a discount rate, then test the copied formula in the first and last rows.

example.scenario: Quantity is in B2, price in C2, and a discount of 10% is stored in H2. You need revenue after discount for each row.
example.solution: Use =B2*C2*(1-$H$2). With 4 units at $25, the result is $90. Copy down, then verify that B and C row numbers move while $H$2 stays fixed.

sections.heading: Summarize and check the finished workbook
paragraphs: Sort the entire dataset so values stay attached to the correct records. Filters temporarily hide records; they do not delete them. Use a pivot table when the task asks for grouped totals by category or period, and refresh it after changing source data. Conditional formatting highlights a rule; data validation restricts permitted entry. Neither guarantees that a plausible number is correct. Verify totals manually on a small sample, inspect formula errors, label charts and units, and test print area, scaling, repeated headers, and page orientation.
bullets: Practice task: create six sales rows, calculate discounted revenue, total revenue by product, and produce one labeled comparison chart.
Common mistake: typing a total over a formula or including a subtotal twice in a grand total.

terms.definition: A reference fixing only its row or its column, such as A$2 or $A2.
A tool that groups and summarizes source records.
Rules restricting the values a cell accepts.

questions.prompt: Which formula keeps the shared discount cell fixed when copied?
questions.explanation: $H$2 fixes both the row and column of the shared discount assumption.

questions.prompt: Which function counts records satisfying one condition?
questions.explanation: COUNTIF counts matching cells; SUMIF adds matching values instead.

questions.prompt: What should happen after source data for a pivot table change?
questions.explanation: A pivot summary may use cached source data and needs to be refreshed.

questions.prompt: What does filtering normally do to unmatched records?
questions.explanation: Filtering changes which records are displayed, while preserving the underlying records.

questions.prompt: Which action best checks a copied calculation?
choices: Manually calculate a sample and inspect first/last references
questions.explanation: A sample calculation and reference checks test arithmetic and copying behavior.

modules.title: Formatting business documents
modules.summary: Using styles, tables, page layout, and mail merge in business documents.

sections.heading: Structure the document with styles
paragraphs: A business document should have a clear purpose, audience, and hierarchy. Use paragraph styles for headings and body text instead of repeatedly applying font changes. Styles make global changes consistent and can support an automatic table of contents. Paragraph spacing controls space around paragraphs; line spacing controls space within them. Use page breaks to start a new page deliberately. Use a section break when part of a document needs a different orientation, header, footer, or numbering scheme. Repeated blank lines are an unstable layout method.

sections.heading: Handle tables, correspondence, and variable data
paragraphs: Tables align related information using rows and columns; tabs or strings of spaces rarely survive changes reliably. Repeat header rows across pages where appropriate and avoid splitting a short logical record unnecessarily. A business letter needs the requested date, recipient, salutation, message, closing, and sender information in the required format. Mail merge combines a main document with a structured data source to create personalized outputs. Verify field names, filters, and representative records before producing the entire batch.

example.scenario: You need to send a personalized invitation to twelve members from a spreadsheet.
example.solution: Create a main invitation with merge fields for name and event date. Connect the source, preview the first, last, and a record with a long name, then merge to a new output and check pagination.

sections.heading: Inspect the final output
paragraphs: Check spelling and grammar while also verifying meaning, names, numbers, and dates. Automatic correction can change a correct specialized term. Inspect headers, footers, page numbering, margins, widow/orphan control, and table wrapping in print preview. Use meaningful heading structure and alternative text when the output format supports accessibility. Export to the requested format, reopen the exported file, and confirm that links, symbols, and page breaks survived. A file that looks correct in the editing window may produce a different printed result.
bullets: Practice task: format a two-page business report using heading styles, a table, a header, and page numbers; export it as a PDF.
Common mistake: formatting every heading separately, then missing one during a revision.

terms.definition: A reusable collection of paragraph and text-formatting settings.
A division that permits different page-level formatting within one document.
Combining a main document and data records to personalize outputs.

questions.prompt: Which approach best keeps all report headings consistent?
questions.explanation: A heading style applies the same reusable formatting and supports consistent revisions.

questions.prompt: When is a section break especially useful?
choices: A page needs a different orientation or header
questions.explanation: Sections can carry independent page layout, headers, footers, and numbering settings.

questions.prompt: What are the two main inputs to a mail merge?
choices: A main document and a structured data source
questions.explanation: The main document supplies fixed content and merge fields; records supply variable values.

questions.prompt: Why reopen an exported PDF?
choices: To verify the exported layout and content
To convert every page into a spreadsheet
questions.explanation: Export can affect fonts, pagination, symbols, and links, so the final file needs its own check.

questions.prompt: Which method is unreliable for starting a new report page?
choices: A section break for different layout
questions.explanation: Blank paragraphs move when text, fonts, or margins change.

modules.title: Slides that explain the evidence
modules.summary: Building readable slides, labeling charts, and checking the presentation files.

sections.heading: Give each slide a job
paragraphs: Begin with the audience’s decision or question, then outline the sequence before designing individual slides. A title should communicate the point, not merely label a topic. Choose a layout that gives evidence enough room to be read. Theme and master-layout tools keep fonts, colors, repeated elements, and spacing consistent. Avoid manually decorating each slide into a different visual system. Put necessary detail in speaker notes or a supporting handout when allowed; a dense slide is not a substitute for an explanation.

sections.heading: Choose and label visual evidence
paragraphs: Use a bar chart to compare categories, a line chart for ordered time trends, and a scatterplot to explore a relationship between two numerical variables. Label units, periods, categories, and sources. A chart cannot establish causation simply because two values move together. Avoid distorted scales, decorative 3D, tiny legends, and colors that are the only way to identify a series. Crop images deliberately without stretching their proportions, and add alternative text where supported.

example.scenario: A slide shows monthly sales, but the axis omits units and the chart uses a truncated vertical scale to exaggerate a small increase.
example.solution: Label the series and period, choose an honest scale for the comparison, and state the actual change. Explain whether the change is large enough to matter to the business decision.

sections.heading: Rehearse the complete output
paragraphs: Use transitions only when they help show a meaningful change. Excess animation takes time and can distract from evidence. Confirm slide order, readable contrast, embedded media playback, and that linked files will be available on the presentation device. Rehearse with speaker notes, a timer, and the actual permitted equipment. Export a backup if the event permits it and verify that the backup still communicates the essential argument. Check the official guide before assuming internet access, sound, external monitors, or a question period are available.
bullets: Practice task: create five slides explaining a small sales dataset, with a central claim, two evidence slides, a recommendation, and sources.
Common mistake: pasting a full spreadsheet into a slide and assuming the audience can read it.

terms.definition: A shared layout system governing repeated slide formatting.
Supporting presenter information associated with a slide.
The proportional relationship between slide width and height.

questions.prompt: Which chart usually best shows an ordered monthly trend?
questions.explanation: A line chart connects observations in time order, making the trend easier to inspect.

questions.prompt: What is the main advantage of a slide master?
choices: It proves all data are accurate
questions.explanation: Master layouts apply shared visual rules across slides.

questions.prompt: What should a chart label make clear?
choices: Units, period, and meaning of the data
questions.explanation: Units, time periods, series definitions, and sources let an audience interpret the evidence.

questions.prompt: Two variables move together. What can the chart alone establish?
choices: An observed association, not automatic causation
questions.explanation: An association can have other explanations and needs more evidence for a causal claim.

questions.prompt: Which assumption should be checked before a conference presentation?
choices: Internet and audio will be permitted
Every judge uses the same laptop
A screenshot can never be useful
Speaker notes are always visible to the audience
questions.explanation: Permitted equipment and connectivity are event-specific rules, not safe assumptions.

modules.title: Move information between spreadsheets, documents, and slides
modules.summary: Linking, embedding, or copying data between files, and checking what the recipient sees.

sections.heading: Understand what travels with the file
paragraphs: A static copy preserves a snapshot of information. Later source changes do not update it automatically. A linked object refers to a source location and can refresh, but the link may break when a source moves or access changes. An embedded object stores content within the destination file; this can make a package more self-contained but may increase file size. Choose based on the required workflow, not the option that happens to look similar on screen.

sections.heading: Preserve meaning across applications
paragraphs: When moving spreadsheet output into a document or presentation, keep the same units, time period, definitions, and rounding policy. A copied value can look like a percentage while becoming text, or a large number can be truncated by a narrow display. Use destination formatting when it improves consistency without changing meaning. For a mail merge, keep one record per row and stable field headers in the source. Preview unusual names, blank fields, and dates before completing a batch.

example.scenario: A report includes a linked quarterly revenue chart. The spreadsheet is renamed after the report is delivered.
example.solution: The link may stop refreshing. Keep source paths stable when linking is required, or provide a verified self-contained embedded/static version when the deliverable calls for portability. Label the data period and reopen the final files on the intended device.

sections.heading: Open and check the files as a recipient
paragraphs: A final check should follow the recipient’s actions: open the document, read the chart, inspect a cited figure, print or present, and follow a relevant link. Compare totals and labels against the source. Check print areas and page breaks in the document as well as the workbook. In slides, test readability from presentation view. Reopen exported PDFs because they may flatten active objects or change layout. Keep filenames clear, remove temporary working files from the submission package, and submit only the formats requested by the event.
bullets: Practice task: build a spreadsheet chart, place it into a report and a slide deck, change one source value, and observe which outputs update.
Common mistake: checking only the source workbook while the delivered document contains an older copied chart.

terms.definition: Content that refers to an external source location and may update from it.
A snapshot that does not automatically track later source changes.
Deliverable files that carry the information they need without unavailable source paths.

questions.prompt: A static chart copy normally does what after its source changes?
questions.explanation: A static copy is a snapshot; it needs deliberate replacement to show updated data.

questions.prompt: Which risk is specific to a linked external object?
choices: The source path or access may change
It can never display a chart
It always removes all source data
questions.explanation: An external link depends on a reachable source location and appropriate access.

questions.prompt: What must remain consistent when reusing a financial table?
questions.explanation: Changing or losing these definitions can make the reused information misleading.

questions.prompt: How should a mail-merge source normally be organized?
choices: One record per row with stable field headers
Every value in a separate workbook
questions.explanation: A structured table lets the merge system associate each field with the correct record.

questions.prompt: What is a strong final integration test?
choices: Reopen the delivered files as the recipient and compare them to the source
Delete the original totals before checking
questions.explanation: Recipient-side checks reveal stale copies, broken links, unreadable charts, and layout errors.

modules.title: Spreadsheet labs: functions, references, summaries, and charts
modules.summary: Hands-on labs with a downloadable practice file: IF and AND, lookups, PMT and FV, dates, absolute references, multi-sheet formulas, sorting, filtering, pivot tables, calculated fields, grouping, and charts, each with an answer key.

sections.heading: Set up the practice file
paragraphs: Download the practice file [computer-applications-sales.csv](/practice/computer-applications-sales.csv) and open it in Excel or Google Sheets. It has 12 fictional sales records with Date, Region, Rep, Product, Units, and Unit Price in columns A to F, with headers in row 1 and data in rows 2 to 13. Save it as a workbook (.xlsx) before you start, since CSV files do not keep formulas, formatting, or extra sheets.

Work through each lab, then compare your results with the answer key. The function names below match Microsoft Excel; Google Sheets uses the same names for these functions. Use the Production Test Reference Guide named in the current event guide for any required formatting.
steps: In G1 type Revenue. In G2 enter =E2*F2 and fill down to G13.
Format F and G as currency with two decimals.
Freeze the top row so headers stay visible.
In G14 enter =SUM(G2:G13). Check: total revenue is $2,401.25.

sections.heading: Logic, lookups, and references
paragraphs: IF returns one value when a test is true and another when it is false. AND requires every condition to be true; OR requires at least one. Nest IFs, or use IFS, for more than two outcomes. COUNTIF, SUMIF, and AVERAGEIF apply one condition; COUNTIFS and SUMIFS apply several.

A relative reference such as G2 changes when copied. An absolute reference such as $J$1 stays fixed, which you need when every row uses one shared input cell. A mixed reference such as $J1 fixes only the column. Lookups find a value by a key: VLOOKUP(key, table, column number, FALSE) searches the first column of a table for an exact match; XLOOKUP(key, lookup range, return range, "Not found") is more flexible and works in any direction. INDEX with MATCH does the same in older versions.

rows: H: flag sales of $250 or more
I: bonus for South sales of $250 or more
Commission at a rate in J1 (enter 0.05 in J1)
Row 2: $7.00; the reference to J1 must be absolute

example.scenario: Build a price lookup. On a new sheet named Prices, list Notebook 3.50, Pen pack 2.25, and Planner 12.00 in A2:B4. On the sales sheet, look up each product's price.
steps: Fill down. Every result should match column F.
example.solution: Absolute references keep the price table fixed as the formula fills down, and FALSE (or XLOOKUP's default) forces an exact match. If a product is misspelled, XLOOKUP shows "Not found" instead of an error.

sections.heading: Financial and date functions
paragraphs: PMT calculates a loan payment: =PMT(rate per period, number of periods, present value). Enter the loan as a positive present value and Excel returns a negative payment (cash going out), or enter it as negative to get a positive result. =PMT(6%/12,60,-20000) returns $386.66 for a $20,000, 5-year loan at 6%. FV calculates the future value of regular savings: =FV(5%/12,120,-100) returns $15,528.23 for $100 a month for 10 years at 5%. Divide annual rates by 12 and multiply years by 12 for monthly periods.

Dates are stored as serial numbers, so they can be subtracted. TODAY() returns the current date. =EDATE(A2,3) adds three months. =NETWORKDAYS(A2,A3) counts workdays between two dates. =TEXT(A2,"mmmm") returns the month name, which is useful for grouping. =DATEDIF(A2,A3,"d") returns days between dates.

sections.heading: Multiple sheets, sorting, filtering, and pivot tables
paragraphs: Refer to another sheet with its name and an exclamation point: =Prices!B2. A 3D reference adds the same cell across consecutive sheets: =SUM(Jan:Mar!B5). Sort the whole table, not one column, by selecting any cell in the data and using a multi-level sort, such as Region A to Z, then Revenue largest to smallest. Filters hide rows that do not match without deleting them; SUBTOTAL(9,G2:G13) sums only the visible rows.

A pivot table summarizes data by category without formulas. Insert a pivot table from A1:G13, put Region in Rows, Product in Columns, and Revenue in Values (Sum). Group dates by month to see trends. A calculated field adds a formula inside the pivot table, such as Commission = Revenue x 0.05. Refresh the pivot table after changing source data. Outline grouping and the Subtotal command collapse and summarize sorted data.

sections.heading: Charts and checking your work
paragraphs: Choose a column or bar chart to compare categories (revenue by region), a line chart for change over time (revenue by month), and a pie chart only for a few parts of a whole. Add a descriptive title, axis titles with units, and data labels where they help. Remove clutter such as unnecessary gridlines and 3D effects. Move a chart to its own sheet or position it so it prints on one page.

Check every workbook before submitting: compare totals with a quick manual estimate, use Show Formulas to look for typed numbers that should be formulas, search for error values (#N/A, #DIV/0!, #REF!), confirm absolute references after filling, and set the print area, orientation, scaling, and repeated header rows.

practice.task: Using the practice file: (a) Write a formula that returns the total revenue for Casey. (b) Write a formula that counts sales in the East region with at least 50 units. (c) Create a column chart of revenue by product. Which product leads, and by how much over the second?
practice.answer: (a) =SUMIF(C2:C13,"Casey",G2:G13) returns $575.00 (180 + 202.50 + 192.50). (b) =COUNTIFS(B2:B13,"East",E2:E13,">=50") returns 2 (90 pen packs and 55 notebooks). (c) Planner leads with $960.00, which is $183.75 more than Pen pack at $776.25. The chart should have a title, labeled axes with currency, and categories in a sensible order.

terms.definition: A cell reference with dollar signs, such as $J$1, that does not change when copied.
A function that finds a key in one range and returns the matching value from another.
A function that calculates the payment for a loan with constant payments and rate.
An interactive summary that groups and totals data by category.
A formula added inside a pivot table using its fields.

questions.prompt: Which formula keeps the reference to a rate in J1 fixed when filled down?
questions.explanation: $J$1 locks both the column and the row.

questions.prompt: Which returns "Bonus" only when sales are at least 250 AND the region is South?
questions.explanation: AND requires both conditions inside the IF test.

questions.prompt: In =VLOOKUP(D2,$A$2:$B$4,2,FALSE), FALSE means:
questions.explanation: FALSE forces an exact match.

questions.prompt: For a 3-year loan with monthly payments at 4.8% annual interest, the PMT rate and periods are:
questions.explanation: Convert to monthly: rate divided by 12 and years times 12.

questions.prompt: After changing source data, a pivot table must be:
questions.explanation: Pivot tables do not update until refreshed.

modules.title: Document, presentation, and integration labs with a timed production task
modules.summary: Word processing with styles, layout, tables, and mail merge; slides with masters, multimedia, notes, diagrams, and action buttons; linking and embedding across applications; review tools; export; and a timed practice task.

sections.heading: Word processing skills
paragraphs: Use styles (Heading 1, Heading 2, Normal) instead of formatting text by hand. Styles keep formatting consistent, let you change every heading at once, and build an automatic table of contents. Set margins, orientation, and paper size in Layout. A section break lets one part of a document have different orientation, columns, or headers; a page break simply starts a new page. Headers and footers can hold page numbers, which can start at a specific number or use a different first page.

Tables organize data: insert, merge, and split cells, repeat the header row on each page, and align numbers to the right or on the decimal. Tabs with leaders (dots) create neat lists such as a table of contents. Edit with Find and Replace, check spelling and grammar, and use the official Production Test Reference Guide for letter, memo, report, and citation formats required by the event.
steps: Mail merge: start a letter, choose Select Recipients and use an existing list such as the practice sales file.
Insert merge fields, such as "Dear «Rep»," and a sentence using «Region» and «Product».
Preview several records, checking spacing and number formats.
Finish and merge to a new document or to printing, and save both the main document and the result.

sections.heading: Presentation skills
paragraphs: Edit the slide master to set fonts, colors, logos, and layouts for every slide at once. Use layouts with content placeholders rather than loose text boxes. SmartArt and drawing tools create diagrams such as process flows and organization charts; align and distribute shapes for a clean look. Insert images and crop or remove backgrounds; compress pictures to reduce file size. Add audio or video and set it to play automatically or on click.

Speaker notes hold talking points that the audience does not see. Action buttons and hyperlinks jump to a specific slide, such as returning to an agenda. Use simple transitions and animations only where they help explain a sequence. Export as PDF for handouts or as a video when the event requires it, and test the exported file.

sections.heading: Integrate applications
paragraphs: Linking and embedding move data between applications differently. A linked object stays connected to its source file: when the spreadsheet changes, the chart in the document updates, but the source file must travel with the document. An embedded object is a copy stored inside the document: it travels with the file but does not update when the source changes. Paste Special offers both choices, along with pasting as a picture or as values.

Review tools support collaboration. Track Changes records every edit so others can accept or reject it. Comments ask questions without changing text. Compare merges two versions. Before final export, accept or reject all changes, delete comments, inspect the document for hidden personal information, and proofread once more on paper or at a different zoom level.

example.scenario: A manager wants a one-page report with a chart that will update when next month's sales are added to the workbook.
example.solution: Create the chart in the spreadsheet, copy it, and use Paste Special, Paste Link in the document. Keep both files in the same folder. When the workbook changes, update the link in the document. If the report will be emailed without the workbook, embed the chart or paste it as a picture instead, accepting that it will not update.

sections.heading: Timed production practice
paragraphs: Production tests reward accuracy and following directions under time pressure. Read all instructions before starting, note every required element, and save often with the required file names. If a step is unclear, complete what you can and keep moving.
steps: Workbook (15 minutes): from the practice sales file, add the Revenue column, a South bonus flag, a pivot table of revenue by region and product, and a column chart of revenue by region.

Report (15 minutes): write a one-page memo to the sales manager in the reference guide's memo format, with a heading style, a two-sentence summary, a table of the top three sales, and the linked chart.
Presentation (10 minutes): build three slides on the master (title, results with the chart, next steps) with speaker notes and an action button returning to the title.
Review (5 minutes): check spelling, formulas, links, file names, and that each requirement is met; export the memo as PDF.

practice.task: Complete the 45-minute task above, then self-check: total revenue $2,401.25; South revenue $675.00; top three sales Planner (Blake) $300.00, Pen pack (Blake) $270.00, Planner (Avery) $264.00; two South bonus rows. List any requirement you missed and the reason.
practice.answer: A complete submission matches every figure above, uses formulas rather than typed totals, follows the memo format exactly, links (or embeds, if instructed) the chart, uses the slide master consistently, includes speaker notes and a working action button, and saves files with the required names. Common misses are forgetting to refresh the pivot table, leaving tracked changes visible, and typing values where formulas were required. Record misses to target in the next timed practice.

terms.definition: A saved set of formatting applied to text consistently across a document.
A break that lets parts of a document have different layout settings.
The template controlling the design and layouts of all slides.
Content that stays connected to its source file and updates when the source changes.
A copy of content stored inside a file that does not update from its source.
A feature that records edits so they can be reviewed, accepted, or rejected.

questions.prompt: Which feature lets one page of a portrait document be landscape?
questions.explanation: Section breaks allow different layout settings.

questions.prompt: A chart must update automatically when the source spreadsheet changes. Use:
questions.explanation: A linked object stays connected to its source.

questions.prompt: To change the font on every slide at once, edit the:
questions.explanation: The master controls design across all slides.

questions.prompt: Before exporting a final document, you should:
choices: Accept or reject all changes and remove comments
questions.explanation: Final documents should not show review markup.

questions.prompt: Applying Heading 1 style to headings lets you:
choices: Generate an automatic table of contents
questions.explanation: The table of contents is built from heading styles.
